newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai January CPI up 4.3 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Thai January CPI up 4.3 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The Thai consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.3 percent year-on-year in January against 4.8 percent in December, a Commerce Ministry official said on Monday.
The official said the 1990-based index rose to 136.6 in January from its 131.0 level in the same month a year ago.
The January CPI rose 0.2 percent from December when it stood at 136.3, against a 0.1 percent month-on-month decline in December over November, the ministry said.
The Thai Commerce Ministry issued the following economic indicators:
THAI CONSUMER PRICES Jan 97 Dec 96 Jan 96

NOTES: In the food and beverage category, vegetable and fruit prices fell 5.9 percent in December from November, egg, dairy product and fresh food prices declined 1.8 percent, and non-alchoholic drinks dipped 0.2 percent. But bread, flour products, meat, poultry and seafood prices rose 1.0 percent month-on-month.

In the non-food group, costs of medical and personal care services surged 1.3 percent in January over December, transport and communication costs increased 0.6 percent, prices in the clothing category rose 0.5 percent, and entertainment, reading materials and education gained 0.3 percent.
